title: Timed universal simulation with timeout
statement: For every effective machine coding scheme $c$, there is a finite-tape machine $U$ over the Boolean alphabet such that for every Boolean code word $\alpha$ there is a natural number $C$, and for every Boolean input $x$ and deadline $t$, both of the following hold. If the machine decoded from $\alpha$ computes an output $y$ on $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, then $U$ computes $1$ followed by $y$ on $\langle\langle\operatorname{bin}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$ in exactly $C(t+1)^2$ steps; if it computes no output on $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, then $U$ computes the one-bit output $0$ on that input in exactly $C(t+1)^2$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is an effective machine coding scheme
replaced:
For every effective machine-coding scheme $c$, there is a single finite-tape machine $U$
over $\{0,1\}$ such that for every code word $\alpha$ there is a natural number $C$ that
works for every Boolean input $x$ and deadline $t\in\mathbb{N}$. If the machine decoded
from $\alpha$ computes output $y$ on $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, then $U$ computes $1$
followed by $y$ on the nested encoding
$\langle\langle\mathrm{bin}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$ in exactly $C(t+1)^2$ steps. If
no output is computed by the decoded machine on $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, then $U$
computes the one-bit output $0$ on that encoding in exactly $C(t+1)^2$ steps.
